sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid page sier1246 (Hammarström et al.)
sources.note: Zero descriptive references. Subclassification comment: 'Said to be ASLic according to Asonye, Emma Ihechi (2016): 787 and Kamei, Nobutaka (2004): 48 but without pointing to underlying evidence.' Only reference with the sgx code in hh.bib is Nyst 2010 (overview); Kamei 2004 lists 'Sierra Leone Sign' without a code.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Varieties of American Sign Language', section 'Sierra Leonean Sign Language' (raw wikitext); ISO 639-3 record sgx
sources.note: Two sentences: 'a variety or descendant of American Sign Language (ASL) used in schools for the deaf in Sierra Leone, or at least in the capital Freetown'; first deaf schools founded by Andrew Foster or his students. Cites only Ethnologue 25. ISO 639-3 page lists no references.

sources.citation: Lewis, M. Paul, Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2016. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 19th ed. Entry 'Sierra Leone Sign Language' [sgx]. (Internet Archive copy of free-access page)
sources.note: Population 200 (2008 WFD); 'Reportedly 200 deaf signers out of 3,000-5,000 total deaf'; Location: Western Area, Freetown, scattered; Status 6a; Agency: Sierra Leone Association of the Deaf. No linguistic description, no bibliography.
sources.venue: Entry 'Sierra Leone Sign Language' [sgx]. (Internet Archive copy of free-access page)

sources.citation: Kamei, Nobutaka. 2004. Afurika no shuwa gengo [The sign languages of Africa]. Afurika Kenkyū / Journal of African Studies 64: 43-64. (Japanese)
sources.note: Continent-wide inventory. p. 48 (p. 6) has a single sentence on this language: 'シエラレオネの首都フリータウンでは,シエラレオネ手話 Sierra Leone Sign Language が話されている[IEL]' = 'In Freetown, the capital of Sierra Leone, Sierra Leone Sign Language is used [source: Ethnologue]'. No structural information; the words 強勢/アクセント/韻律/音韻 (stress/accent/prosody/phonology) do not occur anywhere in the paper.
sources.venue: Afurika Kenkyū / Journal of African Studies
